newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian opposition leader sees long civil war.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition leader sees long civil war.

text.p: Cambodia faces a long civil war unless Second Prime Minister Hun Sen is prepared to negotiate with loyalist opposition forces, opposition leader Sam Rainsy told an audience in Bangkok on Wednesday evening.
"I think Cambodia is headed for turmoil and a long civil war, there will be no development, no investment, no future or lasting progress unless the rule of law is restored," Rainsy said.

Hun Sen, who had shared power with his rival, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, following United Nations sponsored elections in 1993, seized power on July 6 after two days of bloody fighting in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh.
Ranariddh had left for France before the fighting began. Rainsy has aligned his Khmer Nation Party with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC in opposition to Hun Sen.

Rainsy, who was briefly detained earlier by Thai authorities as he tried to cross into Cambodia, said he had been in contact with opposition commanders in territory they controlled on the other side of the border.
He said forces loyal to Ranariddh in the north of Cambodia and close to the border were preparing to resist an imminent offensive by troops under Hun Sen and his Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
But a miltary solution to Cambodia's current crisis was not possible, Rainsy said.
He called upon the international community to put pressure on Hun Sen to stand down, and to help organise elections so that peace could be restored in Cambodia.
"Nobody is in a position to win but the objective is not to win and to defeat Hun Sen militarily," he said.
"The international community have to put pressure on Hun Sen. We need elections as soon as possible and whoever wins should govern Cambodia."

Hun Sen has pledged to stick to pre-coup plans to hold elections next May. But Rainsy said a ballot could not be free and fair if he remained in power, as his motivation for seizing power was to avoid electoral defeat.
"He (Hun Sen) accepts elections only when he is certain to win. The type of election he is going to organise will be biased and rigged," Rainsy said.

Hun Sen's nomination of current Cambodian Foreign Minister and FUNCINPEC party member Ung Huot as Ranariddh's replacement as First Prime Minister was a sham and would not by recognised by any government respecting international laws, Rainsy said.
